## Muses & Directors

I find the intuitive mind incredibly sexy because I can’t fully follow it. During sex, some of the most "womanly" women I’ve loved have gone through psychic experiences, memories that felt like past lives, and things I had no idea how to explain. One time, Bee said she almost got enlightened, but I came too fast. Woops...

Key could sometimes start talking and somehow teleport me outside the galaxy. I don’t know how else to describe it. Her voice would become so beautiful that I would shed tears that felt super liberating.

Bee could bring out something similar. She could be talking to me for hours on end, but instead of trying to mute her with the TV remote, I felt I was in a timeless dimension of love.

In ordinary life, I sometimes think of the woman as the engine and myself as the steering wheel. I get motivation from her. She is the life force. She brings inspiration, beauty, intuition, creativity, and this feeling that life is worth doing. I help give it direction and make it operational.

The muse gives the director his ineffable inspiration. She sees the big picture or feels something that has not become a plan yet. Then I have a chance to be useful by figuring out the details.

The muse can influence any decision where I ask for help, and also the decisions where she suddenly intuits that she has something important to add. She can lead wherever the man is less sure. She may know more about any particular field, even a traditionally non-feminine one. The way she leads can still preserve the polarity of roles.

Micromanaging everything feels totally different and is not attractive. If she refuses to trust my judgment, or simply takes over with “Let me do it,” I start feeling useless.

“Honey, let me help you with this,” is still sexy. Pushing him out of the way is not.

She can also receive his guidance without pretending he’s always right. She might say, “Thank you, I’ll consider that. What do you think about doing it this way?” It’s a kind of gentle, almost hypnotic leadership. She is still influencing where he goes without turning every disagreement into a contest over who is driving.

In my experience, women often prefer stronger and more direct leadership from a man:

“This is where I want to go. This is what I think we should do. Are you game?”

The woman may argue with the plan, change it, improve it, or refuse it. The masculine charge comes partly from directly offering a direction.

Equality in terms of dignity does not require both people to do every role equally. Relationships work better when each person develops what they are good at, like specialization in any economy. That can be taken too far, of course. I’m not saying women should never learn to drive, nor that men should never cook. But if the man enjoys driving and the woman enjoys cooking, they can both usually do what makes them happiest.

Every respectful leader makes sure to take the other person’s ideas as serious input. Mandar obedeciendo, as the Zapatistas say.

The point is not to tally every act and force the totals to match.
